Two measurements worth keeping, because they aim the next one:

* **`artiLink` reads `y = 0.0000` after the FIRST step, and read exactly that
  before this tranche too** (P8.91c's run, byte for byte the same line).  A link
  that were merely un-accelerated would sit at 3.000; a value of 0 is a link whose
  pose never comes back at all.  `dmaBackArticulationDataLaunch` is refused, and
  it is the first thing to look at — but the cause is not yet established and this
  note does not claim it is.
* **`artiCompanionBox` reads 3.7329, also unchanged**, so the rigid half of the
  scene is unaffected by the articulation work in either direction.

The plan's phase-level done-criterion — "the articulation scene settles" — stands.
What was wrong was attaching it to this tranche.

## P8.92b — `computeLinkAcceleration`, and the `+=` association

forwardDynamic2.cu:1931-2316, into `shaders/npArtiLinkAccel.slang`.  Suite 721 →
**722**; manifest unchanged at **274**; zero new ABI.  The wrapper — the one that
changes the scene's verdict — is P8.92c.

Five sections, four of which look alike: the root's EXTERNAL acceleration, pass
one root-to-leaf, the root's INTERNAL acceleration plus the start of the momentum
bookkeeping, pass two root-to-leaf, and the momentum-conservation tail.

### The two passes are not the same loop, in six places

The port shares one body between them behind an `internal` flag, and the six
differences are what the flag selects.  Each gets **two** mutants — one collapsing
the pass onto the other's behaviour in each direction — and all twelve die:

| | pass one | pass two |
|---|---|---|
| a | reads the parent's `mMotionAcceleration` | …`mMotionAccelerationInternal` |
| b | `mQstZ` | `mQstZIcInternal` |
| c | no Coriolis term | ADDS `mCoriolis` |
| d | ASSIGNS `mJointAccel` | ADDS to it |
| e | stores `mMotionAcceleration` | stores `mMotionAccelerationInternal` |
| f | velocity read at the top of the iteration | re-loaded, and used PRE-update for `preMomentum.bottom` |

And one they share, which is a trap in pass two only: **`jAccel` is taken against
the PROPAGATED parent acceleration, not against the running accumulator the
Coriolis term has already moved.**

### What the fixture found: the `+=` association

The first run was off by up to **eight ULP** in the link block, and it was not
contraction — the module is in `PXG_NOCONTRACT_SHADERS`.  The CUDA writes

```
preMomentum.bottom += inertia * motionVel.top + offset.cross(...) * mass;
```

which is `x + (A + B)`: the two new terms associate with **each other** first and
only then with the accumulator.  The port had `(x + A) + B`, which is the natural
way to write it and the wrong one.  Two places, both fixed, and both get a mutant
that restores the wrong association and dies.

### Sweep: 52/54 killed, two proven equivalences

* **Pass one's `motionVelocities[linkID]` write is dead** — pass two loops over
  exactly the same range and overwrites every slot it touches.  Transcribed
  anyway: the day pass two stops covering the same links, the engine's version is
  the one that stays right.  Pass TWO's write is not dead, and for a fixed base it
  is the only one; removing it dies.
* **Pass one's starting velocity may be read before or after the propagation** —
  the propagation writes dof fields and the link's acceleration, never its
  velocity.  Reading the WRONG link's velocity dies.

Two mutants in the first run came back `SKIPPED` because the `+=` fix had moved
their anchor text.  Per the standing rule they were recorded as untested and
re-anchored rather than counted; both then die.

Suite **722/722 in both memory modes**.

## P8.92a — the bias-force sweep and the parallel-axis theorem

`computeJointTransmittedFrictionForce` (forwardDynamic2.cu:2317) as new module
`shaders/npArtiLinkAccel.slang`, and the free `translateInertia(inertia, mass,
offset)` (forwardDynamic2.cu:1569) as `asmTranslateInertiaMass` beside the rest of
the algebra.  Suite 719 → **721**; manifest unchanged at **274**; **zero new ABI
for the fifth tranche running** — `mBiasForce` (20224), `mMotionAcceleration`
(18688), `mMotionAccelerationInternal` (19456), `mInvInertiaXYZ_invMassW` (27648),
`mAccumulatedPose` (23552), `mParents` (28672) and `mRw_{x,y,z}` were all mapped
in P8.68.

These are the two pieces of `computeUnconstrainedAccelerationsLaunch1T` that stand
on their own.  `computeLinkAcceleration` itself is P8.92b and the wrapper — the
one that changes the scene's verdict — is P8.92c.

### The oracle, and it is a strong one

Everything both bodies are built from is `PX_CUDA_CALLABLE`: `PxQuat::rotate` and
`rotateInv`, `PxVec3::multiply`, `PxMat33::getTranspose` and both `operator*`
forms, `FeatherstoneArticulation::translateSpatialVector`, and the engine's own
`loadSpatialVector` / `storeSpatialVector`.  The expectation is therefore the
engine's arithmetic on the host, compared bit for bit; only the loop's STRUCTURE
is transcribed, which is where every trap lives.

### The traps

1. the sweep is **leaf-to-root and strictly sequential** — each iteration
   accumulates into its parent, which a later one reads as its own `Ia`;
2. the parent's bias force is **loaded at the top**, before this link's own `Ia`
   is stored (the P8.88 read-modify-write shape);
3. the inertia and the mass are **per-component reciprocals with their own zero
   guards** — a static link has `invMass == 0`, which the scene contains;
4. **the dual basis crosses over**: the TORQUE half of the force picks up the
   ANGULAR half of the acceleration, and the LINEAR FORCE half picks up the
   LINEAR half.  A port that keeps them parallel produces plausible numbers;
5. the inertia is applied **in the body frame**,
   `rot.rotate(rot.rotateInv(a.top).multiply(inertia))` — and `multiply` is the
   componentwise product, not a dot;
6. `motionAcceleration` is the **SUM** of the external and internal fields;
7. the root's bias force is **zeroed after the loop**, discarding everything the
   loop accumulated into link 0.

And the sign: `translateSpatialVector(+rw, Ia)`, NOT negated — the opposite of the
acceleration direction.

### The fixture

Three topologies in one warp — a **chain**, a **binary tree** and a **star**.  The
tree is the one that earns its place: with three or more links, links 1 and 2 both
hang off link 0, so an interior node receives TWO accumulations and a port that
assigns where it should add is wrong somewhere other than the root.  Beside that:
link counts 2..7, each distinct from its lane index; a link with `invMass == 0`
and a different one with a single zero inertia component, so both guards fire
alone; a lane whose quaternion is the IDENTITY beside lanes with a general
rotation; both acceleration halves non-zero and different; `mBiasForce` pre-seeded
NON-ZERO so `+=` is distinguishable from `=` and the root's zeroing is a real
change; and the whole link-block region compared byte for byte against `0xAB`.

### Sweep: 32/35 killed, three proven equivalences

Two of them are the same fact, and it is worth recording because it bounds what
this call site can check at all: **`s` is skew, so `s^T == -s`**, and therefore
`s^T s`, `s s^T` and `(-s)^T (-s)` are the same sums of the same products in the
same order — bit-identical, since `(-a) * (-b)` is exactly `a * b` in IEEE.  Both
substitutions survive, and neither is a gap: the skew's SIGN CONVENTION is simply
unverifiable here.  That is the argument for keeping the engine's spelling rather
than "simplifying" to `|t|^2 I - t t^T` — the convention IS load-bearing at
`asmSkewSymmetric`'s other call sites, and this one must not drift from it.  The
nearby mutants that break skewness itself (a diagonal entry; a symmetrised
off-diagonal) were added and both die.

The third: **re-loading the parent's bias force at the store** is equivalent,
because nothing writes that slot between the load and the store — a link is never
its own parent.  Hoisting the load OUT of the loop is not equivalent, and the star
topology is what proves it: several links share one parent, so the second of them
would read a stale value.  Added, and it dies.

Suite **721/721 in both memory modes**.

## P8.91c — `computeMassMatrix1T` — manifest **274**, and P8.40 bites for real

forwardDynamic2.cu:1736-1930, assembled on top of P8.91a/b into
`shaders/npArtiMassMatrix.slang`.  Manifest 273 → **274**, suite 717 → **719**,
the engine's refused-kernel list **228 → 227** with this kernel the one that
leaves, and all 240 steps of the articulation scene still complete.  **Zero new
ABI for the fourth tranche running** — every block field and every record pointer
it touches was already mapped.

### The fault that took the tranche, and the rule it confirms

The kernel passed both fixtures bit-for-bit on the first run and then **segfaulted
the live scene**.  Bisecting it inside the shader, one guard at a time, produced a
result worth writing down precisely:

```
  a = articulations + artiInd * 544
  mmWarpCopyU(load_u64(a + 176), ...)          <-- inside the set-bit walk: FAULTS
  mmWarpCopyU(responseMatrices, ...)           <-- same pointer VALUE, resolved
                                                   before the loop: works
```

A host-side probe (temporarily wired into the launch path) confirmed every input
was correct — `nbArticulations` 1, lane 0 active, `mArticulationIndex` 0, flags
`eFIX_BASE`, `numLinks` 2 — and a shader-side dump confirmed the walk itself:
`fixMask` 1, `lowestSetIndex` 0, the broadcast index 0, and the loaded pointer
`0x…ba00`, which the host could read AND write.  A single four-byte store through
that value from inside the loop still faulted; the identical value resolved
outside the loop did not.

That is **platform rule P8.40** — no chained BDA load inside a loop — in its
sharpest form yet: not a grid-stride loop, not a wrong address, and not a
bounds problem.  A pointer *loaded through* a buffer device address and
dereferenced in the same loop is what llvmpipe cannot do.

The port's answer is to broadcast the **already-resolved pointer** in two halves
instead of the articulation index:

```slang
const int src = pxgLowestSetIndex(m);
const uint lo = pxgShflSyncU(FULL, lane, uint(responseMatrices & 0xFFFFFFFF), src, 32u);
const uint hi = pxgShflSyncU(FULL, lane, uint(responseMatrices >> 32),        src, 32u);
mmWarpCopyU(uint64_t(lo) | (uint64_t(hi) << 32), 0u, 144u, lane);
```

This is the same pointer, not an approximation: `responseMatrices` was set to
exactly `articulations[articulationIndex].spatialResponseMatrixW` for every ACTIVE
lane, and only active lanes can be in `fixMask` — which is what the CUDA's own
`assert(artiInd != invalidArticulationId)` asserts.  P8.91b's zero-walk fixture
was reshaped to the same form, so the idiom under test is the idiom in the kernel.

**Neither fixture could have caught this**, and the note says so rather than
pretending otherwise: the harness allocates its own record table, and the pointer
chain it builds happens to survive the same shape.  The live scene is what found
it — the third time in this chain that the scene has been the oracle a fixture
could not be.

### The seven transcription traps

1. the grid is over **articulation blocks**, `ceil(nbArticulations / 32)`, with a
   SECOND per-lane `active` test — lanes past the end stay in every ballot;
2. `articulationIndex` comes from the **block**, not from the island-node/bodySim
   chain the two kernels before it walk (third kernel, third source);
3. the fixed-base path zeroes the **record** through `warpCopy` and the **block**
   through `zeroSpatialMatrix` — two mechanisms, because one is contiguous and the
   other is a 32-lane interleave;
4. `cfm` is a max over three DIAGONAL entries and **the index pattern differs**:
   `bottomLeft.{c0.x, c1.y, c2.z}` of the inverse inertia at the root,
   `response.column[i][3 + i]` per link;
5. the unit impulse is **negated for the links and not for the root**;
6. `maxLinksInWarp` is a warp MAX, so short articulations keep iterating with
   `thisThreadActive` false rather than dropping out;
7. `response` is left uninitialised for an inactive lane and handed to
   `writeMatrix` anyway; the port zeroes it, which is unobservable because that
   lane's matrix is never staged.

Two things the CUDA leaves lying around are dropped with a note rather than
transcribed: `articulationsInBlock` is computed and never used, and the mixture of
`threadIdx.x` with `threadIndexInWarp` inside the link loop is an engine
inconsistency that is only safe because `blockDim.x == 32` (the P8.88 unification).

### The oracle

Both fixtures compare against **one mirror**, built from
`Dy::SpatialMatrix::operator*`, `PxSpatialMatrix::operator*`, the engine's
`loadSpatialMatrix` / `storeSpatialMatrix` / `zeroSpatialMatrix` in both the
7-column and 6×6 forms, and `refPropagateImpulseW` / `refPropagateAccelerationW`
— which moved into `tests/pxgArtiRefHelpers.h` this tranche so P8.90's fixture and
this one share them instead of transcribing the same twelve lines a third time.
Nothing in the expectation is hand-computed.

The module also joins `PXG_NOCONTRACT_SHADERS`, which P8.91b had deliberately left
it out of: it moved bits then and does dense float work now.  Without it the
six-axis response differs from the engine by one ULP in a few hundred words —
which is exactly what the flag exists for, and what the first fixture run showed.

### Fixture and sweep

`artiMassMatrixBody` drives the body over one warp — 27 live lanes and five past
the end, fixed-base and free-base in the same warp (9 / 18), link counts differing
within it so `maxLinksInWarp` (6) exceeds several lanes' own count, a record index
permutation so no lane writes its own slot, a per-link `cfmScale`, and record link
counts that DISAGREE with the block's.  `artiMassMatrixLaunch` adds the geometry:
130 articulations, grid `num1TBlocks * 2`, block (32, 1, 1), a sixth warp slice
allocated and left poisoned, and an island/bodySim chain filled with values that
would resolve to DIFFERENT records if the kernel used it.

**Sweep 49/52 killed, and all three survivors are proven equivalences:**

* `linkID <= maxLinksInWarp` — the extra pass has an empty ballot and writes
  nothing.  Re-anchored to a stride that stops one link SHORT, which dies.
* the per-dof load ignoring its `dof` bound — the four arrays are only read at
  `ind < dofCount`, so the extra loads are unused; the guard bounds the READ, which
  is why it stays.  Re-anchored to dropping the LAST dof, which dies.
* guarding the `mFlags` READ by `active` — equivalent, but it makes the `&& active`
  in the ballot dead.  The port reads the flags unconditionally exactly as the CUDA
  does, and that is what lets the ballot's guard be tested: the fixture's poison
  flags have the fix bit set, so an inactive lane reaching the walk would resolve
  the invalid articulation id.

Two of the four first-round survivors were **fixture** coincidences of the usual
kind and were removed rather than explained: the free-base flag word was zero (so
`flags != 0` stood in for the bit test), and the guarded flags read made the
ballot's own guard untestable.  Both mutants die now.

Suite **719/719 in both memory modes**; all 21 scenes still green.

**The articulation scene still reports its two step failures**, exactly as the
plan said it would: `computeUnconstrainedAccelerationsLaunch1T` is the last
unmapped kernel of the sequence, so the acceleration that would move the link is
still never computed.  That is P8.92, and it is the one that changes the verdict.

## P8.91b — `writeMatrix`: the first warp-cooperative articulation code

`writeMatrix` (forwardDynamic2.cu:1699), `warpCopy<uint>` (copy.cuh:54) and the
`for (m = mask; m; m = clearLowestSetBit(m))` set-bit walk, as new module
`shaders/npArtiMassMatrix.slang` with `tests/testArtiMassMatrix.cpp`.  Suite
715 → **717**; manifest unchanged at **273**; no new ABI.  `pxgClearLowestSetBit`
joins `pxgSlangWarpInc.slang` — the one warp helper P8.91a deferred, landing now
that it has a caller and a fixture.

### What changes with this tranche

P8.83-P8.90 were one thread per articulation with **no cross-lane traffic**,
which is why none of them touched the P2.1 warp library.  Everything here does,
and the failure mode changes with it: not a wrong offset but a lane-divergence or
mask bug, on a platform where `pxgSyncWarp` lowers to a **workgroup barrier**
because llvmpipe's subgroup is 8.  Barrier uniformity therefore stops being
advisory — every loop containing one is bounded by `countbits(mask)`, and every
call site in the kernel to come sits inside a warp-uniform branch derived from a
ballot or a reduction.  A port that made any of those per-lane would deadlock the
workgroup here while working on a real warp.

### The fixture, and the three coincidences removed before the sweep ran

No engine oracle exists — both functions are `__device__`-only and are pure lane
arithmetic — so this is the P8.73-P8.80 arrangement, and the tranche note says so
rather than presenting the sweep as one.  What carries it is that **the
expectation is a permutation, not a computation**: every active lane's 144 bytes
must appear at that lane's destination and nowhere else, over a whole region that
starts at `0xAB…`, so an extra write fails as loudly as a wrong one.

Three fixture coincidences were designed out rather than discovered:

* a **contiguous** mask makes a lane's rank equal its lane index → all four masks
  are scattered and three have lane 0 clear;
* a destination table in **lane order** makes a permuted scatter look right → the
  slot map is a stride-13 permutation over 40 slots;
* a count that is a **multiple of eight** hides both the `min` and the unsigned
  wrap → the four counts are 21, 5, 0 and 32.

The zero walk's record stride is **192 bytes, not 144**, so the 48 bytes past each
`PxSpatialMatrix` must come back poisoned — which is what makes `warpCopy`'s
`totalSize / sizeof(T)` element count observable rather than merely plausible.

### Sweep: 26/28 killed, and **both survivors are proven equivalences**

The kills cover the rank-versus-lane confusion (from both sides — the shader's use
and `pxgWarpRankInMask`'s inclusive/exclusive boundary), the unsigned wrap in
`off = offset - i`, the staging bound, the pass stride at +1, the 18-lane `uint2`
copy at both boundaries and in its pairing, the pointer's high half, the staging
stride, **both barriers**, all four of `warpCopy`'s loop terms, and every part of
the set-bit walk including `clearLowestSetBit` itself.

The two survivors, with their proofs:

* **`nbToProcess = NbPerPass` (the `min` dropped) DIED** — which is worth
  recording, because the module header had predicted it would be equivalent.  The
  reasoning was half right: a staged matrix and its destination travel in the same
  slot, so a stale slot re-writes an earlier result with its own value and is
  invisible.  What that argument misses is the **first** pass of a call whose
  count is below eight, where the leftover slots have never been written at all
  and the pointer is whatever shared memory happened to hold.  The 5-bit mask is
  exactly that case, and it is what killed the mutant.
* **`isActive` dropped from the staging guard — SURVIVES, equivalent here.**
  Ranks are monotone non-decreasing in the lane index and only step up *after* an
  active lane, so an inactive lane always shares its slot with a **strictly
  higher** active lane; the only exception is the lanes above the top active one,
  whose slot is always exactly one past that pass's `nbToProcess` and is never
  copied out.  So the copied-out image can only change if the same-address
  groupshared race resolves in favour of the *lower* lane.  The guard is
  transcribed anyway, because that resolution is a property of this driver and not
  something the Vulkan memory model promises.
* **A pass stride of SEVEN — SURVIVES, equivalent.**  At pass `i` slot `j` holds
  rank `i + j`, so every copy is a correct pair regardless of the stride, and a
  stride below the window merely repeats work.  A stride of **nine** is the nearby
  mutant that is not equivalent — it skips rank 8 entirely — and it was added and
  died.  The original `i += 1` mutant is equivalent for the same reason and was
  re-anchored rather than counted.

`gpuslang.scan` segfaulted once under `-j4` in `PXG_DEVICE_V2=1` and passed on
re-run — the intermittent from the open-items list, now 3 failures in ~11 full
runs, still unattributed and still not this tranche's.

## P8.91a — the 6×6 matrix-vector product, and the fold made observable on purpose

`PxSpatialMatrix::operator*` (PxSpatialMatrix.h:58) as `asmM6MulVec` in
`shaders/pxgSlangSpatialMatrix.slang`, dumped through the existing
`artiSpatialMatrixBlockIo` entry.  No new module, no new test, no new ABI, manifest
unchanged at **273**, suite unchanged at **715/715** in both memory modes.  This is
the first of three pieces of `computeMassMatrix1T`: the algebra (here), then
`writeMatrix`'s warp-cooperative scatter, then the kernel.

### The indexing, which is the whole trap

```
result[i] = 0.f;
for (j = 0..5)  result[i] += column[j][i] * st[j];
```

The **outer** index walks the result and the **inner** one walks `column`'s FIRST
subscript — so despite the field being called `column`, the contraction is over the
first subscript, i.e. this multiplies by the transpose of the reading a name-driven
port would give it.  For the impulse-response matrices that mistake produces a
plausible-looking wrong answer rather than an obvious one, which is why it gets two
mutants (`abM6Get(m, i, j)` for `abM6Get(m, j, i)`, and `st[i]` for `st[j]`) rather
than one.  Both die.

### The fold lane, and why this tranche went looking for it

P8.87 sharpened P8.84's fourth platform rule into something narrow enough to be
testable: the `x + 0.0` fold is the **driver's**, no shader-level workaround defeats
it, and the seed's sign is washed out by IEEE's `(-0) + (+0) = +0` **unless every
accumulated term in a component is `-0`**.  This function is exactly that shape —
a literal-zero seed and six `+=` terms — so the fixture builds the one input that
exposes it rather than leaving the hazard theoretical:

* **lane 3's entire 6×6 is `+0`**, and
* the spatial vector it is applied to is **entirely negative** (`topLeft.column0`
  and `topRight.column0` overridden to `-0.51 … -5.77`, values deliberately off the
  generator's 0.09375 grid so they cannot coincide with another lane's).

Every product is then `+0 × negative = -0`, all six terms are `-0`, and the folded
result is `-0` where the engine's C++ returns `+0`.  Measured: **exactly six words**,
one per result component.  The tolerance is scoped to those six slots of that one
lane, the count is printed, and **both** bounds are asserted — `> 0` so the lane
cannot silently stop exercising the hazard (or the driver stop folding without
telling us), `<= 6` so the fold cannot spread unnoticed.

### The oracle

`PxSpatialMatrix::operator*` is `PX_CUDA_CALLABLE`, so the expectation is the
engine's own arithmetic on the host over the bytes the engine's own
`storeSpatialMatrix` wrote — the P8.86b arrangement, not a transcription.  The
source vector is taken from the seven-column matrix's own first column, so a helper
reaching into the wrong source lands on numbers from a different decade.

### Sweep

**14/14 killed, no survivors**, forced-fresh (`rm build-gpuslang/shaders/*.spv`
first).  Nine on the algebra — transposed contraction, source-indexed inner term,
un-reset accumulator, subtraction, half-length contraction, half-length result,
swapped input halves, swapped output halves, a permutation inside one half — and
five on the fixture side, including the per-lane output stride left at its old 72.

### What was deliberately NOT added

The plan's P8.91a line also mentioned the small warp helpers.  `lowestSetIndex` and
`warpScanExclusive(mask, lane)` **already exist** in `shaders/pxgSlangWarpInc.slang`
as `pxgLowestSetIndex` and `pxgWarpRankInMask` (the latter's comment already names
its CUDA original), and `clearLowestSetBit` is `v & (v - 1)` with no caller yet.
Landing an untested one-liner ahead of the loop that needs it is the opposite of
this chain's discipline, so it goes in with P8.91b's `writeMatrix`, where a fixture
can drive it.  `warpCopy` likewise: it is a lane-strided copy whose element type is
fixed by its caller, not a warp primitive.

## P8.90 — the impulse-response pair, LIFTED rather than re-ported

`propagateImpulseW_everythingPreLoaded` and
`propagateAccelerationW_everythingPreLoaded` (articulationDynamic.cuh:167 / :206)
— the Featherstone/Mirtich pair `computeMassMatrix1T` calls six times per link.
New module `shaders/pxgSlangArticulationDynamic.slang`; suite 714 → **715**;
manifest unchanged at **273**.

### The bodies already existed, and re-deriving them would have been the mistake

Phase 1 ported both, as `npArtiPropagate.slang` and `npArtiPropagateAccel.slang`,
each with its traps already written down.  The module's bodies are **lifted from
those** — same expressions in the same order — not derived a second time from the
CUDA.

The Phase-1 pair stays put rather than being rewired to call the module, and the
reason is concrete: both are in `PXG_HLSL_ENTRIES` and must keep lowering to
cs_6_0, while the module imports the BDA block layer, which does not lower.  What
keeps the two copies honest is that **the module's fixture compares against the
ENGINE** — `Dy::FeatherstoneArticulation::translateSpatialVector` is
`PX_CUDA_CALLABLE` (DyFeatherstoneArticulation.h:828), as are `innerProduct`,
`cross` and `dot` — where the Phase-1 fixtures compare against a host
transcription.  The lift is therefore checked against a *stronger* reference than
the thing it was lifted from.

### Sweep 24 of 25, and the one survivor was predicted in writing

514 cases over both directions, all four dof counts, 12 words each, **no
signed-zero forgiveness needed**.

**D17 survived: bounding the `jDelta` three-lane dot by `dofCount`.**  That is
trap 5, and the module header states the equivalence *before* the sweep ran — the
lanes at or beyond `dofCount` are zero, so the mask is implicit and bounding the
dot is right today.  What makes this a proof rather than an excuse is its
partner: **D20 — seeding `tJointDelta` from `QMinusSTZ` instead of zero — DIES.**
Together they pin exactly the invariant the header names: the dot is unbounded
because the seeding makes it safe, and the moment the seeding changes it stops
being safe.

**D21 was a bug in the sweep, not a result.**  The first attempt mutated which
`invStISW` row is read for `ind >= dofCount` — a branch that never executes, so
the mutant changed nothing.  Per the standing rule it was recorded as untested,
re-anchored to actually drop the guard, and it dies; a second mutant dropping the
*first* pass's guard was added at the same time and dies too.

The fixture's cases exist for the traps rather than for coverage: a **non-zero**
`qstZ` seed, because the CUDA's own caller passes zeros and cannot tell
"accumulates" from "assigns"; **loud** `QMinusSTZ` lanes past `dofCount`, which is
what gives D17/D20 their meaning; a zero-offset stripe where the negation's sign
is invisible beside a majority where it is not; and motion matrices whose halves
differ in magnitude so the dual product and the Euclidean one cannot coincide.

Suite **715/715** in both memory modes, forced-fresh.

## P8.89 — the 6×6 `PxSpatialMatrix` block layer

The response matrices `computeMassMatrix1T` writes are the **full 6×6**
`PxSpatialMatrix` (`PxReal column[6][6]`), not the seven-block `Dy::SpatialMatrix`
P8.86 covers, and their block form is a different packing.  This tranche lands the
three helpers and the one address that was missing.  Suite unchanged at
**714/714**; manifest unchanged at **273** — a helper tranche, and the last one
before the articulation chain starts using real warp cooperation.

### The packing is FLAT, unlike the seven-column one

`PxgSpatialMatrix6x6Block` is `float4 columns[9][32]` — 36 floats chunked four at a
time at the usual lane stride of 32, with `columns[k]` holding flat indices
`4k .. 4k+3` and flat `f` being `column[f / 6][f % 6]`.  No implied block, no
interleaving: 4608 bytes of straightforward SoA.  `abLoadSpatialMatrix6x6`,
`abStoreSpatialMatrix6x6` and `abZeroSpatialMatrix6x6` all have `PX_CUDA_CALLABLE`
originals (PxgArticulation.h:141 / 163 / 176), so the fixture is P8.86b's
arrangement exactly — the engine writes the image, our loader reads it, and the
components are compared against the engine's own loader.  Never a round trip
through our own store.

### The one new address, and why guessing it would have been wrong

`PxgArticulation::spatialResponseMatrixW` had no constant.  **The plan predicted it
between `pathToRoot` (272) and `spatialTendonParams` (304); it is at 176** — off by
a hundred bytes.  Generated, `static_assert`ed in `testNewArticulations.cpp` beside
`jointForce`, and it is exactly the P8.49a failure mode (shader and fixture sharing
one wrong number) that generating it closes.  `sizeof(PxSpatialMatrix) == 144` and
`sizeof(PxgSpatialMatrix6x6Block) == 4608` are pinned with it.

### Sweep 14 of 14, after the sweep found three fixture weaknesses

The first pass was 11/14 with one skipped anchor and two survivors, and **all three
were the fixture, not the code**:

* one anchor matched twice — the store and the zero helper share a loop header —
  so it was **untested, not passed**, and was re-anchored to include the store's
  own body;
* **zeroing the whole block instead of one lane's nine slots survived**, because
  the fixture drove all 32 lanes: the union of every lane's slots *is* the whole
  block, so the two are indistinguishable.  The test now drives **21 live lanes and
  leaves 11 poisoned**, and the mutant dies;
* **`abM6Get`'s row-major convention survived** because nothing called it — the
  entry point dumped the flat array directly.  It now dumps *through the accessor*,
  and the transposed mutant dies.

That is the standing rule holding for the ninth tranche running: a survivor is
almost always a coincidence in the fixture, and the fix is to remove the
coincidence rather than to explain it.

Suite **714/714** in both memory modes, forced-fresh.

## P8.88 — the articulated-inertia sweep + its kernel — manifest **273**

forwardDynamic2.cu:1580-1697.  The leaf-to-root propagation that reduces each
link's articulated inertia by P8.87's term, translates the remainder into the
parent's frame and accumulates it there, then inverts the root — plus
`computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunch1T`, the kernel around it.  Manifest
272 → **273**; suite 712 → **714**; the engine's unmapped-kernel list **229 →
228**, and the one that left is this kernel.

**Third tranche in a row with zero new ABI.**  P8.84's delta was four descriptor
constants, P8.86's and P8.87's were none, and this one's is none either — the
question the plan posed after P8.84 ("will the rest of the articulation block keep
needing new address maps?") is answered, and the answer is no.

### What is transcribed rather than tidied

* **The loop is a genuine dependency chain.**  A link's own inertia has already
  been increased by its children in earlier iterations, which is what makes the
  single descending pass correct — `parents[linkID] < linkID` is the engine's
  invariant.  The mutant that runs it root-to-leaf dies, as does the one that skips
  link 1.
* **Every parent field is read at the TOP of the iteration**, before anything is
  written.  A port that re-loads at the store is right *for the wrong reason*; the
  order is kept, and the tranche note says why the sweep cannot tell them apart.
* **`PxMax(0.f, x)` is `a < b ? b : a`, not `max`.**  PhysX's spelling returns 0
  for a NaN because the comparison is false; Slang's `max` lowers to `OpFMax`,
  whose NaN behaviour is the other way round.  The engine's form is written out.
  The fixture **asserts the clamp actually fires** — it does, twice — so the guard
  is exercised rather than merely present.
* **The CUDA re-loads the parent's two ZA vectors right after storing them and
  never uses either result.**  Dead code; the port drops it and the mirror drops it
  too, rather than transcribing a load nobody reads.

### The kernel's three differences from P8.85's wrapper, each a mutant

1. **Block (32, `1`, 1) and grid `num1TBlocks * 2`** — one warp per block, twice
   the blocks.  `ASI_WARPS_PER_BLOCK` was deliberately left per-kernel in P8.85 for
   exactly this; the fixture's 130 articulations give `num1TBlocks == 3` and a grid
   of 6, and the mutant that reuses 2 visits warp slices 0, 2, 4 only.
2. **`numLinks` comes from the BLOCK**, the opposite of P8.85's record read.  The
   fixture's records carry `0xFEE0 + k` — never a plausible link count — so the two
   cannot agree by accident.
3. It hands the loop the record's `jointForce` pointer, which the loop then offsets
   **per link by that link's own `jointOffset`**, not by the link index.

### The fixture, and one mirror for three users

`testArtiPropagateInertia.cpp` now holds three tests over ONE transcription of the
per-dof algebra: `apiMirror` (P8.87), `apiLoopMirror` wrapping it in the CUDA's
loop, and the two P8.88 tests calling that.  The three `static __device__` helpers
the engine keeps in forwardDynamic2.cu moved to `tests/pxgArtiRefHelpers.h` so
P8.86's fixture and this one share them instead of holding a copy each.

The topology is deliberately **not a straight chain**: `loopParent` returns a
parent `< linkID` that is only equal to `linkID - 1` by coincidence, so a port that
assumes the obvious chain accumulates into the wrong link.  Joint types cycle
through all five — asserted, not assumed — so every branch of P8.87's switch runs
*inside* the loop, and the dof cursor advances by each joint's own dof count.  Link
counts run 1..6, including the **one-link** case where the loop body never executes
and only the root inverse runs, and the base is fixed on a third of the
articulations so both root branches are exercised.

### Sweep 35 of 36

Two mutants did not compile on the first pass — `pblk` and `globalWarpIndex` are
declared after the lines they were anchored to — and per the standing rule a
non-compiling mutant is **not** a kill: both were re-anchored to a real hazard (the
dof count read as a word rather than a byte; the lane taken from the block index)
and both then died.

**One survivor, proven equivalent:** re-loading the parent's inertia at the store
instead of reading it at the top.  Nothing between the two writes that field — the
stores in between are the parent's ZA vectors — and the loop is strictly
sequential, so the two spellings cannot differ.  It is kept in the read-first form
because the equivalence depends on the loop's sequencing rather than on anything
local.

Suite **714/714** in both memory modes, forced-fresh.  All 21 scenes green.  The
articulation scene completes its 240 steps with no fault under `PXG_SYNC_EACH=1`
and its refused-kernel list shrinks by exactly this one — **but its two step checks
still fail, on purpose**: `computeMassMatrix1T` and
`computeUnconstrainedAccelerationsLaunch1T` are still unmapped, so the acceleration
that would move the link is still never computed.  The first tranche that can
change the scene's verdict is the one that lands the last of those.

## P8.87 — `computeIs` + `computePropagateSpatialInertia_ZA_ZIc`

forwardDynamic2.cu:1345-1544 — the per-dof algebra that turns a link's articulated
spatial inertia into the term the parent's inertia is reduced by, and accumulates
the joint's contribution into the zero-acceleration force vectors on the way past.
New module `shaders/npArtiPropagateInertia.slang`; suite 711 → **712**; manifest
unchanged at **272 of 501** — this is the second of the three tranches under
`computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunch1T`, and **zero new ABI** again.

### The oracle, stated honestly

Both CUDA functions are `static __device__` and unreachable from the host, so this
is the P8.73-P8.80 arrangement and not P8.86's: the mirror is the CUDA's **control
flow** with the engine's arithmetic and the engine's block writers inside it —
`SpatialMatrix::operator*`, `innerProduct`, `PxMat33::getInverse`, both
`constructSpatialMatrix` forms, `loadSpatialVector` / `storeSpatialVector`.  Every
one of those got its own fixture in P8.86, so what this tranche tests is the control
flow, which is exactly what the sweep attacks.

One engine duplication was named rather than reproduced: the local
`constructSpatialMatrix(Is, stI)` at :1367 is byte-for-byte the body of
`SpatialMatrix::constructSpatialMatrix(SpatialVectorF, SpatialVectorF)` at
DyFeatherstoneArticulationUtils.h:364.  The port has one function and a note.

### The traps, and the one that is worth the tranche on its own

* **`PxMat33 invStIs(PxIdentity)` starts as the IDENTITY, not zero.**  A two-dof
  spherical joint never writes the third row or column, so those entries stay
  `(0,0,1)` and the matrix inverts.  Seed it from zero and it is singular,
  `getInverse` returns the identity, and every number downstream is wrong — silently,
  because the shape is right.  The fixture has one-, two- and three-dof spherical
  lanes and the mutant dies on the two-dof one.
* **It inverts with `PxMat33::getInverse`, not `invertSym33`**, and the engine's own
  commented-out `//invStIs = SpatialMatrix::invertSym33(invStIs);` sits above it.
  P8.86 measured why that matters; the substitution dies here in situ.
* **`qstZ` ignores the joint force and `qstZIcInternal` uses it** — with the engine's
  commented-out `//link.qstZIc[ind] = jF[ind] - stZ;` right there to make "fixing" it
  look right.  Both directions die.
* **`stI` swaps the halves** (`(Is.bottom, Is.top)`), and the spherical case spells
  the same swap as "columns 0..2 from `.bottom`, 3..5 from `.top`".  Both die.
* **`iStIs = stIs > 0 ? 1/stIs : 0`** — `> 0`, not `!= 0`.  The fixture drives `stIs`
  exactly to zero on one lane and negative on another, and **asserts the sign it
  computed** rather than assuming it; that assertion caught a lane whose dense
  default happened to land negative when it was meant to be positive.
* The write-back is **transposed**: dof `ind2` takes row `ind2` of the inverse.
* The `default` case (`eFIX`, `eUNDEFINED`) writes **nothing**, which the poison
  proves; a lane with `eUNDEFINED` and a *non-zero* dof count pins that it is the
  switch and not the count that selects it.

### Sweep 54 of 55, and what the two survivors taught

The first run was 53/55 with two survivors, and **neither was an equivalence — both
were fixture weaknesses, and fixing them changed the tranche's conclusions.**

**P32 — dropping the inner `ind < dofs` guard — survived because the entry point
seeded `Is[3]` with zeros.**  The CUDA leaves those entries *uninitialised*; zeros
made an unguarded read harmless.  The entry point and the mirror now seed the same
**non-zero poison**, and the mutant dies.  A control mutant that changes the poison
in the shader only confirms the seed is never read by correct code.

**P47 — seeding the seven accumulators with `-0` — survived, and chasing it
overturned what this tranche had already written down about P8.84's rule.**  Three
measurements, in order:

1. A literal-zero seed and P8.84's `abs(x) * 0.0f` runtime-zero seed produce the
   **same SPIR-V `OpFAdd` count (12)**, and the fixture was green either way.  The
   first conclusion drawn — "no fold happens here" — was **wrong**, and it was wrong
   because the fixture could not see the fold.
2. **The seed's sign is washed out by IEEE itself.**  `(-0) + (+0) = +0`, so one
   ordinary term erases it.  A three-dof spherical joint with a diagonal `invStIs` —
   the obvious construction, and the fixture's lane 6 — contributes a `-0` first term
   and then wipes it on the next iteration.  That is why P47 survived and why the
   hazard looked absent.
3. The shape that **does** expose it is a **one-dof spherical joint whose `Is` is all
   negative zeros**: exactly one accumulated term, nothing to wash it out.  Lane 10
   builds that from a zero spatial inertia (a massless link) against an all-negative
   motion matrix, and it **fails immediately** — twelve words, every one `00000000`
   against `80000000`.

So the fold is real, it is the **driver's** and not slangc's, and P8.84's runtime-zero
remedy does not defeat it — re-measured here, unchanged output.  The resolution is
P8.84's other one: a tolerance scoped to `0x00000000` vs `0x80000000` and nothing
else, with the count printed and bounded, plus an assertion that the count is
**non-zero** so the lane cannot silently stop exercising the hazard.  P47 then
survives *by construction*: the driver discards the seed, so the seed's sign has no
observable effect — which is the same fact the tolerance encodes.

**The correction is worth stating plainly**: this tranche's module header first
claimed the fold did not occur, on the strength of an `OpFAdd` count.  An op count
was the wrong instrument; only a fixture that can observe the difference settles it,
and building one took a mutant surviving to prompt it.

### ABI and shape

No manifest row, no ABI row, no new descriptor or block constant: `mWorldMotionMatrix`
1152, `mIsW` 3456, `mIsInvDW` 2688, `mQstZ` 640, `mQstZIcInternal` 768,
`mInvStIsT_{x,y,z}` 4992/5120/5248, the armature at `mConstraintData` 5440 +
`mArmature` 5376, `mJointType` 28832 and `mDofs` 28800 were all already mapped.
`jF` is carried as a device address where **0 means NULL**, the natural port of the
CUDA pointer, and the mutant that reads one as the other dies.

Suite **712/712** in both memory modes, forced-fresh; all 21 scenes unchanged and the
articulation scene's unmapped-kernel list still reads **229**, as a module tranche
should leave it.

## P8.86 — the spatial-matrix algebra layer

`Dy::SpatialMatrix` and the `PxMat33` arithmetic it is built from, ported once as a
module rather than transcribed per kernel: **`shaders/pxgSlangSpatialMatrix.slang`**,
with `abLoadSpatialMatrix` / `abLoadPxMat33` added beside the store twins P8.84
landed.  Suite 709 → **711**; manifest unchanged at **272 of 501** — this tranche
maps no kernel, it is what the next two are built out of.

Everything remaining in the articulation solver stands on this: `computeIs`,
`computePropagateSpatialInertia_ZA_ZIc`, `computeArticulatedSpatialInertiaW` and the
whole impulse-response chain.  Thirty-two operations, one module, one fixture.

### The cleanest oracle in the chain so far

Every operation has a `PX_CUDA_CALLABLE` counterpart the fixture **calls** —
`PxMat33`'s operators, `Dy::SpatialMatrix`'s operators, `invertSym33`,
`invertInertia`, both `constructSpatialMatrix` forms, and
`Cm::UnAlignedSpatialVector::innerProduct / dot / cross`.  Nothing about the
arithmetic is retyped into an expectation; the expectation *is* the engine.

Two exceptions, stated rather than glossed: `translateInertia`
(forwardDynamic2.cu:1546) and `constructSkewSymmetricMatrix` (:1561) are
`static __device__` and unreachable from the host.  Their host mirrors are five
lines of structure over the engine's own `PxMat33` operators — the arithmetic is
still the engine's, only the ORDER is transcribed, and that order is exactly what
trap 5 is about, so the sweep attacks it directly (S46-S51, all dead).

### Two fixtures, and how a wrong SLOT fails as loudly as a wrong number

`artiSpatialMatrix` is table-driven: 32 opcodes × 127 cases, one thread each.  The
output buffer is uploaded **pre-filled with a per-case, per-word poison pattern**;
the shader loads it, writes only the slots its opcode owns, and stores it back.  So
an operation that writes a slot it does not own fails, one that writes the right
value into the wrong slot fails twice, `translateInertia` leaving `topRight` alone is
*checked* rather than assumed, and the `.w` of every output `float4` is a further
poison word that must survive.  4064 cases × 60 words, **zero signed-zero
forgiveness needed** — every word bit-identical.

`artiSpatialMatrixBlockIo` pins the two new loads, and deliberately **not** by
round-tripping through our own stores: a load and a store wrong in mirrored ways copy
perfectly.  The ENGINE's `storeSpatialMatrix` / `storePxMat33` build the block image,
our loaders read it, and the components are compared against what the ENGINE's own
`loadSpatialMatrix` / `loadPxMat33` return from the same bytes.  The same dispatch
also re-stores the loaded matrix through `asmStoreSpatialMatrix` into a second,
poisoned block, compared whole against the engine's `storeSpatialMatrix` image of the
engine-loaded matrix — that wrapper hands three separate `AbMat33`s onward, so a
permutation in the forwarding compiles, and two mutants say so.  All 32 lanes carry
different matrices and every one of a lane's 27 + 9 values is distinct, so a
transposition, a lane-stride error and a packing error land on different numbers.
The packing's one unused word — `columns[6][lane].w`, which the engine's store
zeroes — is **overwritten with poison after the store**, so a loader that reads it
produces garbage instead of a zero it could get away with (S62 dies on exactly that).

### The stripes, and the coincidences they exist to rule out

The standing rule from eight earlier tranches is that a survivor is nearly always a
fixture coincidence.  Here they are specific and each gets a stripe: an **exactly**
singular `M` (column 1 zeroed, so both determinants are exactly +0 and both inverses
take their identity branch — near-singular proves nothing, both sides take the other
branch); a symmetric `M` *and* a non-symmetric majority; a symmetric `A.topLeft`,
which is the only place `transform` and `transformTranspose` agree; an
**antisymmetric** `A.bottomLeft`, which makes `(bl + bl^T) * 0.5` exactly zero so
`invertInertia` reaches `invertSym33`'s identity branch INTERNALLY — the fixed-base
case, through the real call chain; zero-`v.top` and zero-`v.bottom` stripes; and zero
and negative scalars.  Every stripe period (7, 11, 13, 17, 19) is odd and the opcode
count is 32, so each stripe reaches every operation instead of clustering.

### Sweep 73 of 74, and the one survivor is proven equivalent

No build failures, no skipped anchors.  One mutant is the control that asks whether
the poison comparison is vacuous — dropping the store entirely — and it dies, so the
block image really is being checked.  The five named traps all die, and so does
`S09` — `dot` re-associated as `x + (y + z)` — which is the evidence that the fixture
is genuinely bit-sensitive and not merely close.

**S43 survived: `invertInertia` using `PxMat33::getInverse` instead of `invertSym33`
for `AAInv`.**  That is an equivalence, not a hole, and it was measured rather than
argued: `aa` is symmetrised on the line above, and on a symmetric input the two
routines are the same expression up to exactly-rounding identities — the products are
the same pairs (`c1.z*c2.y` vs `c2.y*c1.z`), the negated spelling `-(A - B)` equals
`B - A` exactly, and `x * r` equals `r * x`.  A host probe over **200 000 random
symmetric matrices (1.8 M words) found zero differing words, not even in the sign of a
zero**; the same probe on non-symmetric inputs differs in a third of all words.

The sharp corollary is that **S44 — the same substitution for `LL` — DIES.**  The
Schur complement `S = ll + z·laᵀ` is *not* symmetric (only `ll` was symmetrised), so
`invertSym33` there is not a general inverse and is not interchangeable.  That is
trap 3 as a live measurement rather than a comment: the spherical-joint path in P8.87
must use `getInverse`, and this path must not.

### What is deliberately not here

No manifest row, no ABI row, no new descriptor constant.  P8.84's delta was four
descriptor constants; this one's is zero, and P8.88's will be zero too — every field
`computeArticulatedSpatialInertiaW` touches is already mapped.  That is the answer to
the question this plan posed after P8.84 and it is *no*: the articulation block does
not keep needing new address maps.

Suite **711/711** in both memory modes, forced-fresh.  All 21 scenes unchanged: the
articulation scene still completes its 240 steps with no fault under
`PXG_SYNC_EACH=1`, its unmapped-kernel list still reads **229** (a module tranche maps
nothing), and its two step checks still fail for the reason P8.85 records —
`computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunch1T`, `computeMassMatrix1T` and
`computeUnconstrainedAccelerationsLaunch1T` are still unmapped, so the acceleration
that would move the link is never computed.

## P8.85 — the spatial-inertia wrapper — manifest **272**

`computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunchPartial1T` (forwardDynamic2.cu:1312-1343),
twenty-five lines around P8.84's function.  Manifest 271 → **272**; suite 708 →
**709**; the engine's unmapped-kernel list **230 → 229**, and the one that left is
this one.

**The tranche's real job is not the twenty-five lines.**  P8.84 handed `gravity`,
`dt` and `isExternalForcesEveryTgsIterationEnabled` to the function through push
constants, so their descriptor offsets — 52, 48 and 68 — were pinned by
`static_assert` and by nothing else.  Here they are read out of a real
`PxgArticulationCoreDesc` for the first time, and four mutants say so: gravity read
one component late, gravity read backwards, `dt` read from `invLengthScale`'s slot
at 64, and the flag read one byte late.  All four die.

**The flag is a `bool`, one byte at 68**, and bytes 69..71 are structure padding
before `impulses` at 72.  The fixture memsets the whole descriptor to `0x5A` before
filling it, so those padding bytes are *not* zero — which turns "read it as a word"
from an accident that happens to work into a mutant that dies.  It does.

### Three differences from the velocity kernel's wrapper, each a mutant

The two kernels launch with the same geometry and read the same first three hops,
which makes the places they diverge exactly the ones a copy gets wrong:

1. **This one does NOT write `solverBodyIndices`.**  The velocity kernel writes it
   on every dispatch.  The fixture leaves that array poisoned and requires every
   slot back at `0xAB` — a stronger check than a right value in a right slot, and
   free.
2. **`numLinks` comes from the RECORD**, unconditionally: no refill guard, no block
   fallback.  The fixture seeds the block header with `0xFEED` so the two disagree,
   and the mutant that reads the block dies.
3. **`artiBlock` advances by ONE block per warp** while the link and dof arrays
   beside it advance by `maxLinks` and `maxDofs`.  Both the "no offset" and the
   "offset by a pitch" mutants die.

### The mirror was hoisted rather than copied

`testArtiSpatialInertia.cpp` already held a mirror of the CUDA built entirely from
`PX_CUDA_CALLABLE` engine calls.  It is now a file-static function taking per-warp
and per-articulation **slices**, and both tests in that translation unit call it —
the per-link body test and this wrapper test.  A second copy would have been the
transcription this chain exists to avoid; a header for two callers in one directory
would have been ceremony.  The hoist was verified as behaviour-neutral before the
new test was written: same fixture, same 7 forgiven signed-zero bytes, still green.

Geometry is P8.83's, and for P8.83's measured reason: **130 articulations, three
blocks of (32, 2, 1), five live warp slices, two allocated and left poisoned.**  At
two blocks a warps-per-block of 1 maps block 1's first warp onto a slice block 0
has already filled with identical data — idempotent, and the mutant survives.  At
three it leaves a hole.  `W1` dies here.

`ASI_WARPS_PER_BLOCK` is deliberately **per-kernel and not hoisted into a shared
header**: the next two kernels in this launch sequence
(`computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunch1T`, `computeMassMatrix1T`) run with block
(32, **1**, 1) and twice the grid, so a shared constant would be wrong for them by a
factor of two.

**Sweep 22 of 22, no survivors and no equivalences to explain.**  ABI row is the
existing `kOnePtr` (`{ 8 }`); manifest hand-edited.

Suite **709/709** in both memory modes, forced-fresh.  The live scene completes its
240 steps with no fault under `PXG_SYNC_EACH=1`, and its two step checks still fail
exactly as before — on purpose: `computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunch1T`,
`computeMassMatrix1T` and `computeUnconstrainedAccelerationsLaunch1T` are still
unmapped, so the acceleration that would move the link is never computed.  The first
tranche that can change the scene's verdict is the one that lands the last of those.

## P8.84 — `computeSpatialInertiaW`, and a fourth platform rule

forwardDynamic2.cu:1114-1310 — the per-link body of
`computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunchPartial1T`, and the largest single block
of real numerics in the articulation chain.  Suite 707 → **708**; manifest
unchanged at **271 of 501** (the wrapper is P8.85).

**Two things made this cheaper than it looked, both checked before the code was
written rather than discovered during it.**  Every block field it writes —
`mSpatialArticulatedInertia`, `mIsolatedInertia`, `mMass`, `mZAVector`,
`mZAIntVector`, `mCoriolis`, `mBiasForce`, `mInvInertiaXYZ_invMassW` and the
articulation block's `mCOM_TotalInvMassW` — was **already mapped** by the
wholesale generation in P8.67/P8.68, so the ABI delta is four constants
(`dt` 48, `gravity` 52, `isExternalForcesEveryTgsIterationEnabled` 68,
`zAForces` 88) and two new accessors.  And the oracle is back, stronger than
P8.81's: `Cm::transformInertiaTensor` is `PX_CUDA_CALLABLE`, and so are
`storeSpatialMatrix`, `storePxMat33` and `storeSpatialVector`, so the fixture
builds the **entire expected block image — arithmetic and SoA packing both — by
calling the engine** into a real `PxgArticulationBlockLinkData` on the host, and
compares bit patterns.  Neither the maths nor the packing is retyped as a
literal anywhere.

New module `npArtiSpatialInertia.slang` in `PXG_NOCONTRACT_SHADERS`, plus
`abStoreSpatialMatrix` (7 × float4, the `Dy::SpatialMatrix` packing) and
`abStorePxMat33` (4+4+1 floats, so the third array's element stride is FOUR
where the first two are sixteen).  Both carry their matrices as an `AbMat33` of
three **columns**, because `PxMat33::operator[](i)` returns column *i* and
Slang's `float3x3` indexes rows first — a convention clash that would otherwise
have to be remembered at every call site.

### A fourth standing platform rule: `x + 0.0` is folded away, and that is not IEEE

The first run failed on seven bytes, every one of them `0x80` against `0x00`:
**negative zero against positive zero, all on the two static links**.

Measured, in two layers:

* **slangc** compiles `float3 acc = float3(0,0,0); acc += v * m;` to SPIR-V
  containing the multiply and **no `OpFAdd` at all**, at `-O0`.  The shader now
  seeds those accumulators from a *runtime* zero (`abs(dt) * 0.0f`, which does
  survive), and `spirv-dis` confirms the `OpFAdd` is then emitted.
* **The result is still `-0`.**  That is the proof that a second fold happens
  *below* SPIR-V, in the driver's algebraic pass, where this port has no reach.

The fold is wrong for exactly one input: IEEE says `(-0) + (+0)` is `+0`.  It is
reachable here because a static link has `m == 0`, and every `something * m` is
then a signed zero whose sign follows `something`.  The engine's C++ performs
the add; the shader cannot.

The fixture therefore forgives **exactly** this: compared word by word, a
mismatch is accepted only when both words are `0x00000000` or `0x80000000`, and
the count is printed (7).  Poison against a written zero still fails, and so
does every real value.  The shader keeps the runtime-zero seeding even though
this driver folds it anyway, because that makes *our* artifact correct — the
residual is the driver's.  The earlier articulation modules are green because
their fixtures never produce a negative zero as an accumulator's first term, not
because they are immune; any future accumulator in this port starts from
`asiRuntimeZero()`.

### The convention that flips, and the CUDA's own names being wrong

`Cm::UnAlignedSpatialVector` means (angular, linear) for a **motion** and
(linear force, torque) for a **force** — the Featherstone dual basis, and
correct.  What is *not* correct is the CUDA's local naming in the Coriolis
block: the variables are literally called `force` and `torque` and hold an
angular and a linear **acceleration**, stored top/bottom in that order.  A port
that "fixes" either naming by swapping slots looks plausible and is wrong; both
directions are mutants and both die.

### Sweep: 47 of 49, and the fixture work that got it there

The first sweep killed **42**.  Six of the seven survivors were the fixture:

* **five of them in one block.**  `damped` was a single bool setting *both*
  damping coefficients, which made `linDamping > 0 || angDamping > 0` and `&&`
  the same predicate and left four mutants alive on the coincidence — the guard,
  the `min(coeff, invDt)` clamp (both coefficients were below `invDt`), and the
  angular cap's threshold (no magnitude lay *between* the two caps).  Replaced
  by five damping modes (none / linear only / angular only / both / both above
  `invDt`) and six velocity modes, with the mode coverage **asserted**: the test
  fails if any mode stops occurring.
* **two survivors needed searched inputs, not chosen ones.**  `v * (1/m)` and
  `v / m` round identically for every round-numbered velocity, and
  `sqrt(cap)/sqrt(mag)` and `sqrt(cap/mag)` for every round-numbered cap.  A grid
  search found `(0.125, -0.125, 0.75)` for the first and `angCap = 0.65` against
  a magnitude-squared of `1.625` for the second.  The reciprocal mutant then died.

One survivor was a **sweep bug** and is recorded as untested: `zDamp += X` where
`zDamp` is zero-initialised is `zDamp = X`, so the mutant changed nothing.
Re-anchored to seed `zDamp` from `zExt` instead of zero, which dies.

**The two remaining survivors, measured rather than excused:**

* `S31`, `sqrt(cap/mag)` for `sqrt(cap)/sqrt(mag)`.  The searched pair differs by
  1 ulp under glibc's `sqrt` on the host — and produces **identical bits on
  llvmpipe** for every (cap, magnitude) pair in the fixture, across 17 links and
  two passes of a byte-exact comparison.  So the difference is real in principle
  and this driver's rounding hides it.  The port uses the engine's spelling.
* `S49`, reverting the runtime-zero seeding.  Equivalent *on this driver* by
  construction — it is the fold described above — and included in the sweep on
  purpose, as the check that the workaround's cost is understood.

Suite **708/708** in both memory modes, forced-fresh.

## P8.83 — `computeUnconstrainedVelocities1TLaunch` assembled — manifest **271**

Twelve tranches after the articulation dynamics were opened, the first real
articulation solver kernel is mapped.  Manifest **270 → 271**; suite 706 →
**707**; the engine's unmapped-kernel list **231 → 230**, and the one that left it
is this one.

**The wrapper is composition, not transcription, and that was the point of every
tranche since P8.74.**  Every part of `computeUnconstrainedVelocitiesInternal1T`
is already a Slang *function* with its own fixture and its own sweep, so the entry
point is 60 lines of index chain, per-warp bases and guards over eleven calls.
Phase A was the last piece still living inside its entry point; it is now
`jcalcRecomputeRecord` — and its two flags are **parameters**, which is
load-bearing rather than tidy (see below).

**The launch shape, and a stale comment in the engine.**
`PxgArticulationCore.cpp:437` launches block **(32, 2, 1)** with
`num1TBlocks = (nbArticulations + 63) / 64`.  The comment beside it says "each
warp will work on one articulation"; the code says
`globalThreadIndex = threadIdx.x + globalWarpIndex * WARP_SIZE` guarded by
`< nbArticulations`, which is **one thread** per articulation.  The grid
arithmetic settles it — 64 articulations per block, not 2 — so the code is right
and the comment is not.  No barriers and no groupshared anywhere in the kernel,
which is why the divergent early return is safe on llvmpipe.

**Three orderings the wrapper has to get right, none of which any phase fixture
could have caught:**

1. **`confiDirty` is read once, before phase A clears it.**  The CUDA reads it
   into a local at :372, phase A writes `artiData.confiDirty = false` at :429, and
   the branch at :436 tests the **local**.  A body that re-read the record would
   skip phase B on exactly the frame that needs it.  Same shape for
   `refillBlockData`, computed from the block's `mArticulationIndex` *before*
   `jcalcFillBlockHeader` overwrites it.
2. **`updateDirty` is read before `jcalcRefreshBlocks`, which clears it.**  The
   engine's `else if (dataDirty)` branch runs the refresh, *then* the three
   tendon/mimic updates guarded by bits of `updateDirty`, and only then zeroes it
   (:751).  Our refresh function clears it at its own end — that is what its own
   fixture pins — so the guards must use the saved value.
3. **The per-warp bases are not one pitch.**  Attachments are
   `maxSpatialTendons * maxAttachments` per warp, tendon joints are
   `maxFixedTendons * maxTendonJoints`, and the bitfields are
   `maxLinks * wordSize` with `wordSize = (maxLinks + 63) / 64`.

ABI row `{ 8, 1, 1 }` → a 16-byte blob, the first row in the table with **two
adjacent one-byte arguments**; both bools come out of one push-constant word with
a shift, the way `broadphaseEndPtHistogram` does for its one.  One new constant,
`PXG_BODY_SIM_SLEEP_THRESHOLD = 104` — a *derived* offset (`.z` of the float4 at
96), so it is pinned in its own right rather than left as "96 + 8" at the call
site.  Manifest hand-edited, as always.

### The fixture, and the four survivors that turned into fixture work

`testArtiUnconstrainedVel` drives the whole kernel on the engine's own launch
geometry.  It does **not** re-derive the eleven phases' field-level expectations —
that would be the second transcription this chain has spent twelve tranches
avoiding.  It checks what only the wrapper can get wrong (the three-hop index
chain, `solverBodyIndices`, the nine per-warp bases, the guard order, the launch
shape), one witness per composed piece, and two allocated-but-unreached warp
slices that must come back entirely 0xAB.

**The first sweep killed 28 of 42.  Every one of the fourteen survivors was
examined, and eleven of them were the fixture, not the shader** — the sixth
consecutive tranche where that is the finding:

* **four pitches were equal.**  `maxSpatialTendons == maxFixedTendons == 2` and
  `maxAttachments == maxTendonJoints == 3`, so a base built from the wrong one was
  a no-op.  All seven pitches are now distinct.
* **`wordSize` was 1.**  With `maxLinks = 3` the bitfield base's `* wordSize` is
  the identity.  `maxLinks = 65` makes it 2.
* **one tendon of each kind.**  The element index is `t * maxElements + j`, so a
  single tendon puts everything at slot 0 whatever the pitch is.  Two tendons with
  two elements each, and the attachment / tendon-joint regions are now compared
  slot-by-slot against poison.
* **the fifth guard case was missing.**  Every `confiDirty` lane also had
  `refillBlockData` true, so re-reading `confiDirty` after phase A cleared it
  changed nothing.  A lane with `confiDirty` set *and* a matching cached block
  index discriminates it.
* **the record was never read back.**  `updateDirty` is cleared by the refresh and
  by nothing else, and `confiDirty` by phase A and nothing else — reading both
  back separates "the refresh ran" from "the fill ran" and gives phase A a witness
  at wrapper level.
* **the ABI bools were only ever launched as zero.**  Three passes now:
  `(0,0)`, `(1,0)`, `(0,1)`.
* **ONE BLOCK.**  This is the interesting one.  `blockIdx.x * blockDim.y` is zero
  in a single block whatever the multiplier is.  At **two** blocks a multiplier of
  1 maps `(block 1, warp 0)` onto warp slice 1 — which block 0 already covered with
  the same data — so the duplicated work is *idempotent* and the mutant still
  survives.  Only at **three** blocks does the wrong multiplier leave a hole:
  warp indices 0,1,1,2,2,3 cover threads 0..127 and articulations 128 and 129 are
  never processed.  130 articulations, three blocks, five live warp slices.

One survivor was a **sweep bug** and is recorded as untested rather than counted:
`lane = globalThreadIndex & 31` is bit-for-bit `groupThreadId.x & 31`, since
`globalThreadIndex = x + warp * 32`.  Re-anchored to `lane = globalWarpIndex & 31`,
which dies.

**Second sweep: 40 of 42, and both survivors are proven equivalent by argument
rather than excused:**

* `V40`, dropping the **second** `mFlags` write (:584).  Its guard
  (`confiDirty || refillBlockData`) is the same predicate as the header fill's
  (`refillBlockData || confiDirty`), the source is the same `data.flags` byte, and
  phase A does not touch it.  It is redundant *today*; it is transcribed because
  the CUDA has it and because "redundant" becomes "load-bearing" the moment either
  guard changes upstream.  No mutant can tell the difference and the port says so.
* `V42`, decoding `directAPI` from the whole push-constant word instead of its low
  byte.  `directAPI` is consumed by exactly one callee, `jcalcRefreshBlocks`, which
  runs only when `refillBlockData` is false, which requires
  `forceRecomputeBlockFormat` false, which means bits 8..15 are zero — and the CUDA
  blob's bytes 10..11 are zero-filled padding.  So on this kernel `word != 0` and
  `(word & 0xff) != 0` are equivalent *by the branch structure*, not by the ABI.
  The masked form stays, because the equivalence is a property of a downstream
  branch and not of the argument encoding.

### Verification, including the part a fixture cannot do

Suite **707/707** in both memory modes, forced-fresh.  And the live scene, which is
the oracle this tranche actually turns on: `PXG_GPU_STEP=1 PXG_SCENE=articulation`
now reports **230** "Could not find registered CUDA function" names instead of 231,
with `computeUnconstrainedVelocities1TLaunch` the one that left, the 240 steps
still completing, and no fault under `PXG_SYNC_EACH=1`.  The scene's two step
checks still fail exactly as before — unchanged on purpose: the kernels that
consume what this one produces (`computeUnconstrainedSpatialInertiaLaunch1T`,
`computeUnconstrainedAccelerationsLaunch1T`) are still unmapped, so nothing reads
its output yet.  What changed is that its launch is no longer refused.

**A note for the next sweep.**  Piping the sweep script through `head` kills it
with SIGPIPE mid-mutant: `atexit` restores the *source* but the mutated `.spv` is
left on disk, and the next test run fails against a shader that no longer matches
any source.  Read the full output or redirect it; do not truncate it.

## P8.82 — the rest of the `PxgArticulationCoreDesc` map, and one duplicate collapsed

P8.81 closed with "what remains is the wrapper, the ABI row and the manifest entry
(P8.82)".  Reading the wrapper first turned up something that had been glossed:
**only seven of the descriptor's fields were mapped.**  P8.66 mapped exactly what
`dmaArticulationResidual` addressed and no more, which was right at the time;
`computeUnconstrainedVelocities1TLaunch` addresses seventeen more.  Folding an
address map into the assembly tranche is the one thing this chain has consistently
refused to do, so it is its own tranche and the assembly moves to P8.83.

Suite **706/706**, unchanged — this adds no test *suite*, it extends the one that
already owns this descriptor.  Manifest unchanged at **270 of 501**.

**Seventeen constants, all generated, none in the order a reader would guess.**  The
throwaway host program emits `offsetof` against the real header for each; three of
the results are things transcription would have got wrong:

* **`mPathToRootBitFieldBlocks` is at 176 — *before* `mArticulationDofBlocks` (184)
  and every tendon block pointer.**  The header declares it in the middle of the
  temp-bitfield group, nowhere near the block pointers the launch code uses it
  alongside.  A port that lays the constants out in the order the wrapper *reads*
  them puts it after the tendon blocks.
* **The pitches are not in launch order either**:
  `mMaxMimicJointsPerArticulation` (256) sits between `mMaxDofsPerArticulation` (252)
  and `mMaxSpatialTendonsPerArticulation` (260).  Four of the seven land one slot off
  if the declaration order is assumed to match the usage order.
* **`invLengthScale` (64) follows `gravity`, a `PxVec3`** — it is precisely the field
  a wrong `sizeof(PxVec3)` assumption lands on, and 60 vs 64 vs 68 cannot be settled
  by reading the struct.  Both wrong answers are mutants below.

The gaps are deliberate and accounted for in the module comment (dt 48, gravity 52,
the external-forces bool 68, the impulse/slab/partition group 72..127, the traversal
stack 144 and the three *temp* bitfield pointers 152/160/168).  Two of the gaps are
traps rather than blanks: **200 and 224 are the tendon CONSTRAINT block pointers**,
which bracket the tendon block pointers this tranche does map.  They stay unmapped —
this port adds a constant when a kernel needs it — but they are now pinned by
`static_assert` anyway, so a header change that shifts them fails the build instead
of silently re-aiming `SPATIAL_TENDON_BLOCKS` and `TENDON_JOINT_BLOCKS` at the wrong
arrays.

**A `static_assert` is not enough here, and saying why is the point of the probe.**
The assert proves the constant matches the header.  It says nothing about whether the
*shader* reads at the offset it names — a constant used at the wrong call site
type-checks perfectly, and seventeen of these have no kernel behind them yet.  So
`dmaArtiResidualBda.slang` gains a second entry point, `artiCoreDescProbe`, which
reads all **24** mapped fields through their named constants and writes the raw bits
out in a fixed slot order.  The fixture fills every mapped field *through its real
C++ member* with a value no other field carries, memsets the rest to `0x5A`, and
derives the expectation **out of the struct** rather than restating it — a restated
expectation and a wrong constant can agree.  A swapped pair of constants then yields
a *different field's* value; a constant aimed into a gap yields the poison; two
trailing poison slots catch a probe that writes one entry too many.

The fixture sets the member with `reinterpret_cast<decltype(probe.f)>(...)`, so it
never names the fourteen block struct types and cannot pick the wrong one for a
field.

**The duplicate is gone.**  `PXG_AR_LINK_SIZE` (pxgSlangArticulationBlocks) and
`PXG_ARTI_LINK_SIZE` (pxgSlangArticulationDesc) were both 80, generated independently
into two modules — P8.74's `N18` swapped one for the other and nothing happened,
which is what a duplicate looks like right up until the day one is regenerated and
the other is not.  The blocks-module copy is deleted and `npArtiBlockProbe` (which
already imports both modules) now uses the surviving one.  Mutant `C17` mis-sizes it
to 88 and kills `artiBlockLayout` and `newArticulations` together, which is the proof
that the collapse did not quietly orphan a call site.

**Sweep: 23 of 23, no survivors and no excuses.**  Sixteen mutants move a single
constant onto a plausible neighbour (the `invLengthScale` 60/68 pair, the two pitch
swaps, each block pointer onto the pointer before or after it, the two tendon
CONSTRAINT pointers); one mis-sizes the collapsed stride; six attack the probe itself
— reading a pitch as a pointer, a pointer as a `u32`, emitting two slots in the wrong
order, dropping a slot so everything after shifts, writing one slot too many, and
duplicating a read.  Every one dies.

Suite **706/706** both memory modes, forced-fresh.  What remains for
`computeUnconstrainedVelocities1TLaunch` is now only the composition, the `{8,1,1}`
ABI row and the hand-edited manifest entry — **P8.83, 270 → 271**.

## P8.81 — the fused C2P + link-velocity loop, and the oracle comes back

forwardDynamic2.cu:971-1053, the last piece of real work in
`computeUnconstrainedVelocitiesInternal1T` and the **only part of it with actual
numerics** rather than data movement.  Suite 705 → **706**; manifest unchanged at
**270 of 501**.  One new ABI constant, `rootPreMotionVelocity` at 104, generated and
pinned.

**The oracle is back.**  Every tranche since P8.69 compared against a *transcribed*
expectation, because `jcalc` and its neighbours are `__device__`-only.  This one is
different: `Cm::UnAlignedSpatialVector::rotate` is `PX_CUDA_CALLABLE`, so the fixture
computes the expectation **by calling the engine** — its `rotate`, its
`PxVec3::cross`, its `PxMin`/`PxAbs` — on the host and compares bit patterns.
Nothing about the maths is transcribed, and it was bit-exact on the first run.

**Four behaviours transcribed rather than tidied, each with its mutant dead:**

1. **Two passes, not one.**  The clamp ratio is the minimum over *every* dof and only
   then applied.  The fixture puts the tightest limit on the **last** dof, so a fused
   single pass scales the earlier ones by 1 and fails.
2. **`dofs` is a running cursor**, driven by the link block's `mDofs` (phase B2
   filled it), not indexed by a joint offset.  Dof counts are 2/1/3 — all different
   and none equal to its `linkID`.
3. **The root's `mPreTransform` is a raw `float4` copy of `mAccumulatedPose`, `p.w`
   included; every other link goes through `storeSpatialTransform`, which writes
   `p.w = 0`.**  The fixture puts a non-zero value in every accumulated pose's `p.w`,
   so the root's must survive and the links' must not.  **Both** mutants die — the one
   that unifies on the store path and the one that unifies on the copy path.
4. `rootPreMotionVelocity` is written **through the record**, not the block.

**Sweep: 19 of 20, and the survivor is proven equivalent by measurement.**

`U16` (mRw_y/mRw_z swapped) survived the first pass and was a **real fixture gap**:
link positions were built as `(fv(4), fv(5), fv(6)) * 8`, a linear ramp, so the
per-component offsets were the same constant for every link and
`rw = p_child - p_parent` came out with `rw.y == rw.z` *exactly*.  Different
multipliers plus a quadratic term break the cancellation and the mutant dies.  That
is the fifth fixture coincidence this chain has surfaced — and the first one that was
an arithmetic degeneracy rather than an equal size or a zeroed neighbour.

`U19` (dropping the `jVel != 0` guard on the clamp) survives, and the reason is
measured, not assumed:

* with a **non-zero** limit, `k / |0| = +inf` and `min(ratio, +inf) = ratio` — the
  guard is provably a no-op;
* the only input that could discriminate it is a **zero limit on a zero-velocity
  dof**, i.e. `0/0 = NaN`.  That case was added to the fixture explicitly, and the
  mutant **still** survives: llvmpipe's `min` returns the non-NaN operand.

So the guard cannot be discriminated on this driver at all.  It stays, for two
reasons: the CUDA has it, and SPIR-V's `FMin` with a NaN operand is *not* specified
to behave the way `NMin` does — this is a driver behaviour we measured, not a
guarantee we can port on.

Suite **706/706** both memory modes.  With this, everything
`computeUnconstrainedVelocities1TLaunch` is made of is ported; what remains is the
wrapper, the ABI row and the manifest entry (P8.82) — **270 → 271**.

## P8.80 — `initialize()` and the block-header fill

The two functions that bracket `jcalc` inside
`computeUnconstrainedVelocitiesInternal1T`: the header fill (:941-957, guarded by
`refillBlockData || confiDirty`) and `initialize()` (:62-102).  Suite 704 → **705**;
manifest unchanged at **270 of 501**.

There is no arithmetic here at all — the entire risk surface is that between them
these two functions touch **four element strides in one basic block**:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| `PxU32[32]` / `PxReal[32]` | 4 bytes | the counters and header words |
| `PxU8[32]` | 1 byte | `mStateDirty` — four lanes per word, so the atomic pair |
| `float4[32]` | 16 bytes | `mDeltaQ` |
| pointer `[32]` | 8 bytes | `mMotionVelocitiesPtr` |

**The one non-zero write in a function whose entire job is zeroing** is `mDeltaQ`,
set to the **identity quaternion `(0,0,0,1)`**.  A `memset`-shaped port yields a zero
quaternion — not a rotation at all — and nothing complains until something rotates by
it.  Both mutants aimed at it die: zeroing it outright, and putting the 1 in `x`.

No new ABI.  `mSleepThreshold` comes from
`bodySim.freezeThresholdX_wakeCounterY_sleepThresholdZ_bodySimIndex.z` and
`PxgBodySim` is already mirrored in `pxgSlangCommon.slang`; `articulationIndex` and
the sleep threshold are **parameters** rather than record reads, because both are
resolved by the launch wrapper — which is what keeps the function composable for
P8.82.

**Sweep: 16 of 16 — after two fixture fixes, both of them the same lesson again.**
The first pass was 14/16:

* *"the per-link loop runs over `totalDofs`"* survived because the link block array
  was allocated at exactly `numLinks`, so the extra iterations wrote **past the end
  of the checked region** and the comparison never saw them.  Sizing the array past
  `numLinks` (6 blocks for 3 links) kills it.  **An overrun has to land somewhere the
  test looks** — poison only proves anything inside the region you read back.
* *"`flags` read as a word instead of a byte"* survived because the record was
  `memset` to **zero**: `flags` is a `PxU8` at offset 26 with `confiDirty` at 27 and
  `numPathToRoots` at 28, so a word read there returned `flags` exactly.  Poisoning
  the record to 0xEE kills it.  That is the **fourth** time in this chain a
  convenient zero or a coincidental equality has hidden a mutant — after `nbDof`'s
  zeroed neighbours (P8.72), `mNbElements == maxNumAttachments` (P8.78) and
  `numLinks == totalDofs` (P8.79).

Loop bounds in this fixture are deliberately all different — 5 lanes, 3 links, 6
dofs — for exactly that reason.

Suite **705/705** both memory modes.  What remains: the fused C2P/link-velocity loop
(P8.81, where the engine oracle returns) and the wrapper (P8.82).

## P8.79 — the `gpuDirtyFlag` block, and the refactor it forced

The direct-GPU-API refresh (forwardDynamic2.cu:754-905): the host pokes values
straight into the articulation record and raises bits saying which.  **Ten branches
over nine flags**, then the flag is cleared.  Suite 703 → **704**; manifest unchanged
at **270 of 501**.

**`eDIRTY_POSITIONS` drives two branches**, and separating them is the whole design
of the fixture:

```
POSITIONS                      -> every dof's mJointPositions
ROOT_TRANSFORM | POSITIONS     -> every LINK's mAccumulatedPose, from linkID 0
```

A port that hangs the pose loop off `ROOT_TRANSFORM` alone passes a
root-transform-only case and a velocities-only case and fails positions-only; one
that hangs it off `POSITIONS` alone fails the reverse.  The sub-case matrix runs all
three, and mutants `S1` and `S2` — one for each mistake — both die.  The pose loop
also starts at **linkID 0**, unlike the phase B2 and phase C link loops that start at
1 because the root has no joint; here the root's pose is exactly what a
root-transform poke changes.  `S3` dies on lane-0 link 0.

**The refactor this tranche forced.**  The four tendon branches are the *two halves*
of P8.78's copy functions, **separately guarded** — `eDIRTY_SPATIAL_TENDON` refreshes
only the params, `eDIRTY_SPATIAL_TENDON_ATTACHMENT` only the per-attachment mod
fields — where `jcalc` always runs both.  Rather than transcribe those field lists a
third time, each copy function was split into
`jcalcCopySpatialTendonParams` / `…Attachments` (and the fixed pair), with the
